quote:
Additionally, as we've previously shared, we're building more formal governance within
our board of directors around how we establish our policies in this area and adjust them
over time.
why_new: Searched v2 for board role in setting or adjusting framework policies; v2 only says the Board oversees product and regulatory compliance.

quote:
We currently focus on three
high-level mechanisms, where failure would pose catastrophic risk and the pathways to
such an outcome are identifiable and measurable: one, our ability to understand system
behavior and capabilities before deployment; two, the ability of these systems to bypass
oversight throughout their operation; and three, our ability to prevent and contain
breakout during model training and evaluation.
why_new: v2 scoped only two control mechanisms; containment during training/evaluation appeared only as an illustrative emerging scenario, not an in-scope outcome.

quote:
For Loss of Control 3, we will plan for the assessment to take place prior to model
training or evaluation, which requires prospective assessment: informed estimation of
the expected capabilities of the model being trained or evaluated.
why_new: Searched v2 for any assessment required before training begins or prospective capability estimation; none found.

quote:
The foreseeable high
severity risks identified through this assessment then must be mitigated prior to training
or evaluation.
why_new: v2 ties mitigations to deployment or continued development, never to mitigation before a training or evaluation run starts.

quote:
In both cases, we plan to extrapolate from available data on these evaluations to make
a best-guess prediction of the cyber offensive capabilities of the model prior to training.
Since capabilities are challenging to predict, we will rely on conservative methodology –
for example, pre-RL capability thresholds which appear necessary, if not sufficient, for
high-risk capabilities after RL in our training regime.
why_new: Searched v2 for extrapolation or pre-RL capability forecasting methods; v2 has no prospective prediction methodology.

quote:
A projected pre-mitigation high risk
assessment for Cyber 1 or Cyber 2 may be sufficient for a high risk determination for
Loss of Control 3, while the extent of the mitigations required to sufficiently reduce the
risk depend on the Cyber risk as well as the risk determination for Loss of Control 2.
why_new: No Loss of Control 3 threshold exists in v2; v2 never links cyber results to a containment risk determination.

quote:
For models with cyber
capabilities comparable to models currently considered frontier, environments
used in reinforcement learning or evaluation will run in a sandbox whose
configuration will be approved through a standardized internal process designed
to ensure that they are resistant to realistic attempts by a model at reward
seeking and breakout or with comparable security measures such as hardware
isolation.
why_new: Searched v2 security commitments; v2 covers model weight security only, nothing on sandbox configuration for RL or evaluation.

quote:
We plan to red-team for methods of
external unauthorized action, including cybersecurity vulnerabilities, in all
sandbox configurations before standardization and approval for use in training
and evaluation of near frontier models. All sandboxes with detected high severity
vulnerabilities will be remediated, mitigated with compensating measures such as
hardware isolation, or removed from a reinforcement learning run prior to
initiation.
why_new: v2 red-teaming targets model capabilities and mitigations, not training/evaluation sandboxes; no sandbox remediation requirement found.

quote:
We plan to red-team for problematic reinforcement
learning environments (e.g., those which give the model impossible tasks or are
easily cheated). Environments deemed problematic will be remediated, manually
approved, or removed from a reinforcement learning run prior to initiation.
why_new: Searched v2 for reward hacking measures; v2 only discloses reward hacking in preparedness reports, no RL environment red-teaming or removal.

quote:
In our red-teaming pipelines, we will use models, methods, and compute budgets
proportionate to the projected capabilities of the model, the opportunities for breakout or
reward tampering in the planned training or evaluation run, and uncertainty in those
assessments.
why_new: No v2 standard for sizing red-teaming resources to projected capabilities or breakout opportunities in training runs.

quote:
All model
rollouts must be logged to write-only data stores in real time to preserve their
integrity for analysis and offline monitoring.
why_new: Searched v2 for logging of rollouts or chain-of-thought; v2 mentions logging only as a cyber deployment-level mitigation example.

quote:
All training or
evaluation runs that pose high risk or greater pre-mitigation require
chain-of-thought and trajectory monitoring to be active for all rollouts, with any
exceptions requiring manual approval by the Director of Alignment and Risk or
the Chief AI Officer.
why_new: v2 has no monitoring requirement for training or evaluation runs triggered by a high-risk determination.

quote:
We will develop monitoring systems capable
of rapidly halting individual training or evaluation rollouts when high severity
misbehavior or breakout attempts are detected.
why_new: Searched v2 for automated halting or shutoff of training rollouts; none found.

quote:
We will require that our monitors
pass smoke tests in all sandboxes prior to their use in training or evaluation, in
which they reliably detect attempts to escape by internal models attempting to
escape.
why_new: v2 has no requirement to test or validate monitors in sandboxes before training or evaluation use.
